speaker: Patient
text: 7-year-old boy. The patient has been experiencing recurrent episodes lasting 3–4 minutes each of facial grimacing and staring over the past month. During these episodes, he is nonresponsive and does not recall them afterward. He reports a muddy taste in his mouth before the onset of these episodes. His brother witnessed him waking up, staring, and making hand gestures during one episode. The patient felt lethargic and confused afterwards.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Focal Imminent Epileptic Seizure with Secondary Generalization (specifically an Auras of rising epigastric sensation or 'muddy taste' followed by impaired awareness). The clinical presentation of a 'muddy taste' (dysgeusia) preceding staring and unresponsiveness in a 7-year-old boy is highly suggestive of an autonomic aura associated with temporal lobe epilepsy. The duration (3-4 minutes) and post-ictal confusion are consistent with this diagnosis.
